name: (3-Aminopropyl)triethoxysilane
description: (3-Aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (CAS 919-30-2 ), commonly sourced under the abbreviation APTES, is an aminosilane coupling agent that bridges inorganic surfaces and organic polymer matrices. It bonds to glass, metals, and mineral fillers while presenting reactive amine groups toward resins, adhesives, and coatings, improving interfacial adhesion across composite systems. In fiber-reinforced composites and filled rubber, APTES is applied as a surface treatment for glass fibers and silica, significantly improving mechanical strength and moisture resistance. Epoxy adhesive and sealant formulators use it both as a coupling agent and adhesion promoter, particularly where bonding to metal or glass substrates is critical for the application. In electronics, it functionalizes silicon wafers, sensor surfaces, and printed circuit board substrates to enable controlled deposition of coatings or bioactive layers for advanced devices. Coatings producers incorporate it to improve adhesion of primers and topcoats to difficult substrates, including aluminum and treated plastics, ensuring long-term durability and performance. APTES is supplied as a liquid, typically at 98–99% purity for technical and research-grade applications. It is available in packaging ranging from small laboratory quantities up to bulk drums. No standard food or pharmacopeial grades apply; procurement specifications typically reference purity, amine content, and hydrolysis stability to ensure consistent chemical performance.
